condition.method: Absolute robust z-score against preceding 12 weeks; exploratory thresholds, not regulatory or validated health limits.

model_benchmark.method: The default uses the earlier validation period and minimizes mean normalized RMSE across the three indicators and three native horizons for the whole-lake summary. Pooled zone validation breaks ties. Lower is better. Later scores use the same forecast pairs for every candidate.
model_benchmark.normalization: Pooled zone RMSE uses training-only within-zone temporal deviation; whole-lake RMSE uses training-only whole-lake temporal deviation. All nine tasks have equal weight within each scope.
limitations: Later periods may already have been reviewed during project development; fresh observations are needed for external validation.
Horizon labels correspond to 1, 2 and 4 satellite reading steps, which may occur at irregular intervals.
Whole-lake comparison lines share origin observation weights on the same eligible zones.
The active forecast model is refitted using all available readings after selection. Its future performance and interval coverage are unknown.
Observations beyond 32 days have not been validated. Prophet models calendar days directly; other models interpolate between the native horizons.
The equal-weight consensus was added after seeing the first retrospective comparison. Its current scores are development evidence, not an unseen test.
Seasonal similarity was added during retrospective development and updates only with observations already recorded at each forecast origin.
Prophet was fitted to observed dates through the fitting cutoff. Its historical predictions use nominal calendar leads, and the same recorded targets as the other candidates.

Whole-lake was chosen as the product selection scope after the initial model comparison, because the dashboard opens to the whole lake. The later period is retrospective model development, not a fresh test of this choice.

data_audit.spatial_aggregation: 6 by 6 training-coordinate grid intersected with fixed zones
data_audit.negative_proxy_values_retained: Algorithm and units are unverified; no physical concentration assumption is made.
data_audit.source_zone_ids: Fixed supplied/inferred study-area metadata; no water values used to derive zone IDs.
data_audit.target_definition: Parameter-valid observed source values averaged within each fixed zone. Targets are never filled.
data_audit.source_units: NDWI index and unverified turbidity/chlorophyll proxies; source pixel QA is unknown.

evaluation_meta.evaluation: Origin-safe chronological validation; each native horizon scored independently after model selection is available. Evaluation weights and all-history refit are separate.

refinement.selection_criterion: Mean of nine validation RMSE values (3 parameters x 3 native horizons), each divided by its training-only pooled within-zone temporal standard deviation; every task has equal weight.

last_observed_diagnostic.description: Diagnostic only: exact latest causal observed zone value, with no learned adjustment. This is not a deployed forecasting model.

original_frozen_det.description: Frozen original DET pre-2022 validation audit computed using its own unsnapped preprocessing. Same source-zone target pairs and corrected origin availability; raw errors retained and normalized with current training-zone temporal scales.

calibration.method: Empirical same-selection-validation absolute residual quantiles; not independent calibration or guaranteed coverage. Widths transfer to separately refitted production weights.

production_refit.fit: All historical eligible targets using settings and epoch selected before held-out scoring.

limitations: Turbidity/chlorophyll source algorithms, physical units and satellite QA remain unverified.
The 2022–2023 historical benchmark has already been reviewed during development; fresh independent data are needed for confirmation.
Accuracy is reported separately from successful training; negative R² is retained.
Daily display interpolates native DET outputs. Beyond32days projections are experimental and have no uncertainty bounds.

knowledge.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
knowledge.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

knowledge.title: USGS: Sediment and Suspended Sediment
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Storms transport eroded soil and debris. Moving water carries suspended sediment, which may settle in slower water or be resuspended by faster flow. Rainfall context supports investigating sediment runoff; it does not prove that a lake event was caused by runoff.
knowledge.applicability: General hydrologic mechanism. Local catchment, flow and field measurements are required to test it.

knowledge.title: US EPA: Water Treatment Optimization for Cyanotoxins, Version 1.0
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Nutrients, calm water, temperature and light can favor cyanobacteria growth. Rain can supply nutrients, followed by conditions that support growth. A chlorophyll or algae signal does not establish cyanobacteria species, toxins, or exposure risk; confirmation needs appropriate sampling.
knowledge.applicability: General bloom context, not a calibration for this satellite chlorophyll proxy or a local bloom diagnosis. See source section 2 and Table 2-1.

knowledge.title: Google Earth Engine: Harmonized Sentinel-2 Level-2A Surface Reflectance
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Sentinel-2 surface reflectance includes scene classification for water, cloud shadows, clouds, cirrus and snow. Cloud and shadow detection products assist quality masking. Inadequate clear pixels require inspection before interpreting changes in water indices or reflectance proxies.
knowledge.applicability: Measurement quality context for Sentinel-2. Low coverage is a reason to withhold classification; it does not prove an artefact.

knowledge.title: NASA MODIS surface reflectance quality flags in Earth Engine
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: The MOD09GA product documents surface-reflectance quality information, including cloud state, cloud shadow, land and water flags, aerosol conditions and band quality. These fields support checking observation reliability before interpreting spectral changes. The supplied CSV lacks those QA fields and does not identify its source product.
knowledge.applicability: MODIS quality-control context only. This reference does not establish that the uploaded CSV was extracted from MOD09GA, that its pixels were cloud-masked, or that its turbidity and chlorophyll values have calibrated physical units.

knowledge.title: WHO: Guidelines for drinking-water quality (2022)
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Drinking-water safety requires identifying microbial, chemical and other relevant hazards, water safety planning from catchment to consumer, and independent surveillance. Microbial verification uses faecal indicators such as E. coli. Chemical quality is assessed using water analysis against appropriate guideline values. Appearance or optical indicators alone do not establish drinking-water safety.
knowledge.applicability: General WHO drinking-water assessment framework, including microbial and chemical aspects. It is not a local test result, a complete laboratory panel, or an approval to drink this lake water. Applicable national requirements and the water supplier or health authority govern a local decision.

knowledge.title: CPCB: Water quality criteria for designated uses (Annexure I)
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: CPCB distinguishes drinking-water sources, organised outdoor bathing, wildlife and fisheries, and irrigation uses. Bathing criteria include faecal coliforms, faecal streptococci, pH, dissolved oxygen and biochemical oxygen demand. Wildlife and fisheries criteria include pH, dissolved oxygen and free ammonia. Irrigation criteria include pH, electrical conductivity, sodium adsorption ratio and boron. Drinking-source categories include treatment or disinfection requirements.
knowledge.applicability: Indian designated-best-use criteria in Annexure I. Use the applicable field and laboratory results and official local assessment when interpreting these criteria.

knowledge.title: FAO: Water quality for agriculture — water quality evaluation
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Irrigation assessment considers salinity, soil infiltration, specific ion toxicity and other effects. Electrical conductivity and sodium adsorption ratio are considered together for infiltration; sodium, chloride and boron can affect sensitive crops. Interpretation also depends on soil, crop, drainage, climate and irrigation management. pH is part of the guideline context. Optical lake indices cannot substitute for these measurements.
knowledge.applicability: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1, chapter 1 and Table 1. Agronomic screening, largely developed in arid and semi-arid conditions; it is not a local irrigation clearance or an assessment of microbial risks for food crops.

knowledge.title: CDC: Preventing illnesses caused by harmful algal blooms
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: Check and follow local swimming, fishing and drinking-water advisories. If water has suspicious discoloration, bad smell, foam, scum or algal mats, avoid contact and keep children, pets and livestock away. Rinse with clean tap water after suspected contact. Boiling water containing algal toxins does not remove them and can concentrate them. Contact the water utility or local health/environment authority about concerns. Do not fill pools directly from lakes, rivers or ponds.
knowledge.applicability: Conditional general exposure precautions; this dashboard has not detected a harmful bloom, toxins or an active official advisory. CDC guidance is used as general health context, not as an Indian regulatory standard or proof of a local hazard.

knowledge.title: ESA Lakes CCI: Lake products v3.0
knowledge.text: Paraphrase: ESA Lakes CCI provides satellite lake surface temperature and total suspended matter estimates on a roughly one-kilometre grid. Available observations depend on scene quality and the local extent of open water.
knowledge.applicability: Source context for ESA Lakes CCI lake observations. An uploaded value needs its own source identifier to verify product provenance.

sources.title: NASA MODIS surface reflectance quality flags in Earth Engine
sources.text: Paraphrase: The MOD09GA product documents surface-reflectance quality information, including cloud state, cloud shadow, land and water flags, aerosol conditions and band quality. These fields support checking observation reliability before interpreting spectral changes. The supplied CSV lacks those QA fields and does not identify its source product.
sources.applicability: MODIS quality-control context only. This reference does not establish that the uploaded CSV was extracted from MOD09GA, that its pixels were cloud-masked, or that its turbidity and chlorophyll values have calibrated physical units.

sources.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
sources.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
sources.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

sources.title: US EPA: Water Treatment Optimization for Cyanotoxins, Version 1.0
sources.text: Paraphrase: Nutrients, calm water, temperature and light can favor cyanobacteria growth. Rain can supply nutrients, followed by conditions that support growth. A chlorophyll or algae signal does not establish cyanobacteria species, toxins, or exposure risk; confirmation needs appropriate sampling.
sources.applicability: General bloom context, not a calibration for this satellite chlorophyll proxy or a local bloom diagnosis. See source section 2 and Table 2-1.

sources.title: WHO: Guidelines for drinking-water quality (2022)
sources.text: Paraphrase: Drinking-water safety requires identifying microbial, chemical and other relevant hazards, water safety planning from catchment to consumer, and independent surveillance. Microbial verification uses faecal indicators such as E. coli. Chemical quality is assessed using water analysis against appropriate guideline values. Appearance or optical indicators alone do not establish drinking-water safety.
sources.applicability: General WHO drinking-water assessment framework, including microbial and chemical aspects. It is not a local test result, a complete laboratory panel, or an approval to drink this lake water. Applicable national requirements and the water supplier or health authority govern a local decision.

sources.title: CPCB: Water quality criteria for designated uses (Annexure I)
sources.text: Paraphrase: CPCB distinguishes drinking-water sources, organised outdoor bathing, wildlife and fisheries, and irrigation uses. Bathing criteria include faecal coliforms, faecal streptococci, pH, dissolved oxygen and biochemical oxygen demand. Wildlife and fisheries criteria include pH, dissolved oxygen and free ammonia. Irrigation criteria include pH, electrical conductivity, sodium adsorption ratio and boron. Drinking-source categories include treatment or disinfection requirements.
sources.applicability: Indian designated-best-use criteria in Annexure I. Use the applicable field and laboratory results and official local assessment when interpreting these criteria.

sources.title: CDC: Preventing illnesses caused by harmful algal blooms
sources.text: Paraphrase: Check and follow local swimming, fishing and drinking-water advisories. If water has suspicious discoloration, bad smell, foam, scum or algal mats, avoid contact and keep children, pets and livestock away. Rinse with clean tap water after suspected contact. Boiling water containing algal toxins does not remove them and can concentrate them. Contact the water utility or local health/environment authority about concerns. Do not fill pools directly from lakes, rivers or ponds.
sources.applicability: Conditional general exposure precautions; this dashboard has not detected a harmful bloom, toxins or an active official advisory. CDC guidance is used as general health context, not as an Indian regulatory standard or proof of a local hazard.

sources.title: FAO: Water quality for agriculture — water quality evaluation
sources.text: Paraphrase: Irrigation assessment considers salinity, soil infiltration, specific ion toxicity and other effects. Electrical conductivity and sodium adsorption ratio are considered together for infiltration; sodium, chloride and boron can affect sensitive crops. Interpretation also depends on soil, crop, drainage, climate and irrigation management. pH is part of the guideline context. Optical lake indices cannot substitute for these measurements.
sources.applicability: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1, chapter 1 and Table 1. Agronomic screening, largely developed in arid and semi-arid conditions; it is not a local irrigation clearance or an assessment of microbial risks for food crops.

sources.title: NASA MODIS surface reflectance quality flags in Earth Engine
sources.text: Paraphrase: The MOD09GA product documents surface-reflectance quality information, including cloud state, cloud shadow, land and water flags, aerosol conditions and band quality. These fields support checking observation reliability before interpreting spectral changes. The supplied CSV lacks those QA fields and does not identify its source product.
sources.applicability: MODIS quality-control context only. This reference does not establish that the uploaded CSV was extracted from MOD09GA, that its pixels were cloud-masked, or that its turbidity and chlorophyll values have calibrated physical units.

sources.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
sources.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
sources.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

sources.title: US EPA: Water Treatment Optimization for Cyanotoxins, Version 1.0
sources.text: Paraphrase: Nutrients, calm water, temperature and light can favor cyanobacteria growth. Rain can supply nutrients, followed by conditions that support growth. A chlorophyll or algae signal does not establish cyanobacteria species, toxins, or exposure risk; confirmation needs appropriate sampling.
sources.applicability: General bloom context, not a calibration for this satellite chlorophyll proxy or a local bloom diagnosis. See source section 2 and Table 2-1.

sources.title: WHO: Guidelines for drinking-water quality (2022)
sources.text: Paraphrase: Drinking-water safety requires identifying microbial, chemical and other relevant hazards, water safety planning from catchment to consumer, and independent surveillance. Microbial verification uses faecal indicators such as E. coli. Chemical quality is assessed using water analysis against appropriate guideline values. Appearance or optical indicators alone do not establish drinking-water safety.
sources.applicability: General WHO drinking-water assessment framework, including microbial and chemical aspects. It is not a local test result, a complete laboratory panel, or an approval to drink this lake water. Applicable national requirements and the water supplier or health authority govern a local decision.

sources.title: CPCB: Water quality criteria for designated uses (Annexure I)
sources.text: Paraphrase: CPCB distinguishes drinking-water sources, organised outdoor bathing, wildlife and fisheries, and irrigation uses. Bathing criteria include faecal coliforms, faecal streptococci, pH, dissolved oxygen and biochemical oxygen demand. Wildlife and fisheries criteria include pH, dissolved oxygen and free ammonia. Irrigation criteria include pH, electrical conductivity, sodium adsorption ratio and boron. Drinking-source categories include treatment or disinfection requirements.
sources.applicability: Indian designated-best-use criteria in Annexure I. Use the applicable field and laboratory results and official local assessment when interpreting these criteria.

sources.title: CDC: Preventing illnesses caused by harmful algal blooms
sources.text: Paraphrase: Check and follow local swimming, fishing and drinking-water advisories. If water has suspicious discoloration, bad smell, foam, scum or algal mats, avoid contact and keep children, pets and livestock away. Rinse with clean tap water after suspected contact. Boiling water containing algal toxins does not remove them and can concentrate them. Contact the water utility or local health/environment authority about concerns. Do not fill pools directly from lakes, rivers or ponds.
sources.applicability: Conditional general exposure precautions; this dashboard has not detected a harmful bloom, toxins or an active official advisory. CDC guidance is used as general health context, not as an Indian regulatory standard or proof of a local hazard.

sources.title: FAO: Water quality for agriculture — water quality evaluation
sources.text: Paraphrase: Irrigation assessment considers salinity, soil infiltration, specific ion toxicity and other effects. Electrical conductivity and sodium adsorption ratio are considered together for infiltration; sodium, chloride and boron can affect sensitive crops. Interpretation also depends on soil, crop, drainage, climate and irrigation management. pH is part of the guideline context. Optical lake indices cannot substitute for these measurements.
sources.applicability: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1, chapter 1 and Table 1. Agronomic screening, largely developed in arid and semi-arid conditions; it is not a local irrigation clearance or an assessment of microbial risks for food crops.

sources.title: WHO: Guidelines for drinking-water quality (2022)

Appearance or optical indicators alone do not establish drinking-water safety.

Applicable national requirements and the water supplier or health authority govern a local decision.

sources.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
sources.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
sources.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

sources.title: USGS: Sediment and Suspended Sediment
sources.text: Paraphrase: Storms transport eroded soil and debris. Moving water carries suspended sediment, which may settle in slower water or be resuspended by faster flow. Rainfall context supports investigating sediment runoff; it does not prove that a lake event was caused by runoff.
sources.applicability: General hydrologic mechanism. Local catchment, flow and field measurements are required to test it.

data_audit.spatial_aggregation: 6 by 6 training-coordinate grid intersected with fixed zones
data_audit.negative_proxy_values_retained: Algorithm and units are unverified; no physical concentration assumption is made.
data_audit.source_zone_ids: Fixed supplied/inferred study-area metadata; no water values used to derive zone IDs.
data_audit.target_definition: Parameter-valid observed source values averaged within each fixed zone. Targets are never filled.
data_audit.source_units: NDWI index and unverified turbidity/chlorophyll proxies; source pixel QA is unknown.

metadata.evaluation: Frozen refined DET; settings and epoch selected only with origin-safe 2021 validation; native rolling forecast targets in 2022–2023.

refinement.selection_criterion: Mean of nine validation RMSE values (3 parameters x 3 native horizons), each divided by its training-only pooled within-zone temporal standard deviation; every task has equal weight.

last_observed_diagnostic.description: Diagnostic only: exact latest causal observed zone value, with no learned adjustment. This is not a deployed forecasting model.

original_frozen_det.description: Frozen original DET pre-2022 validation audit computed using its own unsnapped preprocessing. Same source-zone target pairs and corrected origin availability; raw errors retained and normalized with current training-zone temporal scales.

fixes: Six-decimal coordinate canonicalization prevents numerical grid churn.
Validation origins cannot precede training-model availability.
Exact causal observed-zone anchors for residual candidates; learned direct DET heads also evaluated.
Training-only within-zone temporal scales balance the three parameters.

metadata.lake_aggregation: Both actual and predicted summaries use identical parameter-valid source-row count weights at the forecast origin, renormalized over common scored zones. This is not the changing-sample target-date raw lake mean.
metadata.interval_method: No uncertainty bands are claimed for historical comparison.
metadata.errors: error = prediction - actual; metrics.csv pools zones only.
limitations: The 2022–2023 period was reviewed during earlier development. This remains a retrospective benchmark, not fresh external validation.
Current configuration and epoch were locked using pre-2022 validation without scoring post-2021 targets during selection.
Unknown source QA, retrieval formulas and proxy units limit environmental interpretation.
Later observed readings enter rolling input histories only after becoming available. This is not a single year-long forecast.
Negative scores and errors remain visible; no curve adjustment or test-based model selection is performed.

data_audit.spatial_aggregation: 6 by 6 training-coordinate grid intersected with fixed zones
data_audit.negative_proxy_values_retained: Algorithm and units are unverified; no physical concentration assumption is made.
data_audit.source_zone_ids: Fixed supplied/inferred study-area metadata; no water values used to derive zone IDs.
data_audit.target_definition: Parameter-valid observed source values averaged within each fixed zone. Targets are never filled.
data_audit.source_units: NDWI index and unverified turbidity/chlorophyll proxies; source pixel QA is unknown.

training.evaluation: Origin-safe chronological validation; each native horizon scored independently after model selection is available. Evaluation weights and all-history refit are separate.

refinement.selection_criterion: Mean of nine validation RMSE values (3 parameters x 3 native horizons), each divided by its training-only pooled within-zone temporal standard deviation; every task has equal weight.

last_observed_diagnostic.description: Diagnostic only: exact latest causal observed zone value, with no learned adjustment. This is not a deployed forecasting model.

original_frozen_det.description: Frozen original DET pre-2022 validation audit computed using its own unsnapped preprocessing. Same source-zone target pairs and corrected origin availability; raw errors retained and normalized with current training-zone temporal scales.

calibration.method: Empirical same-selection-validation absolute residual quantiles; not independent calibration or guaranteed coverage. Widths transfer to separately refitted production weights.

production_refit.fit: All historical eligible targets using settings and epoch selected before held-out scoring.

limitations: Turbidity/chlorophyll source algorithms, physical units and satellite QA remain unverified.
The 2022–2023 historical benchmark has already been reviewed during development; fresh independent data are needed for confirmation.
Accuracy is reported separately from successful training; negative R² is retained.
Daily display interpolates native DET outputs. Beyond32days projections are experimental and have no uncertainty bounds.
Zone intervals are empirical and can under-cover; lake intervals are not calibrated.

auto.uncertainty: Empirical 80% validation residual intervals transferred from the evaluation model to the all-history production refit. Coverage is not guaranteed; inspect held-out interval coverage. Daily values interpolate between anchors. Long horizons are experimental.
auto.selection_method: The default uses the earlier validation period and minimizes mean normalized RMSE across the three indicators and three native horizons for the whole-lake summary. Pooled zone validation breaks ties. Lower is better. Later scores use the same forecast pairs for every candidate.

data_audit.spatial_aggregation: 6 by 6 training-coordinate grid intersected with fixed zones
data_audit.negative_proxy_values_retained: Algorithm and units are unverified; no physical concentration assumption is made.
data_audit.source_zone_ids: Fixed supplied/inferred study-area metadata; no water values used to derive zone IDs.
data_audit.target_definition: Parameter-valid observed source values averaged within each fixed zone. Targets are never filled.
data_audit.source_units: NDWI index and unverified turbidity/chlorophyll proxies; source pixel QA is unknown.

metadata.evaluation: Frozen refined DET; settings and epoch selected only with origin-safe 2021 validation; native rolling forecast targets in 2022–2023.

refinement.selection_criterion: Mean of nine validation RMSE values (3 parameters x 3 native horizons), each divided by its training-only pooled within-zone temporal standard deviation; every task has equal weight.

last_observed_diagnostic.description: Diagnostic only: exact latest causal observed zone value, with no learned adjustment. This is not a deployed forecasting model.

original_frozen_det.description: Frozen original DET pre-2022 validation audit computed using its own unsnapped preprocessing. Same source-zone target pairs and corrected origin availability; raw errors retained and normalized with current training-zone temporal scales.

fixes: Six-decimal coordinate canonicalization prevents numerical grid churn.
Validation origins cannot precede training-model availability.
Exact causal observed-zone anchors for residual candidates; learned direct DET heads also evaluated.
Training-only within-zone temporal scales balance the three parameters.

metadata.lake_aggregation: Both actual and predicted summaries use identical parameter-valid source-row count weights at the forecast origin, renormalized over common scored zones. This is not the changing-sample target-date raw lake mean.
metadata.interval_method: No uncertainty bands are claimed for historical comparison.
metadata.errors: error = prediction - actual; metrics.csv pools zones only.
limitations: The 2022–2023 period was reviewed during earlier development. This remains a retrospective benchmark, not fresh external validation.
Current configuration and epoch were locked using pre-2022 validation without scoring post-2021 targets during selection.
Unknown source QA, retrieval formulas and proxy units limit environmental interpretation.
Later observed readings enter rolling input histories only after becoming available. This is not a single year-long forecast.
Negative scores and errors remain visible; no curve adjustment or test-based model selection is performed.

hypotheses.name: Runoff or suspended sediment
support: Aligned measured rainfall context is unavailable.
No matching turbidity increase established.
hypotheses.limitations: Co-occurrence is not causal proof. Catchment flow and sediment samples are missing. Rainfall context is used only when supplied in the uploaded measurements.

evidence.title: USGS: Sediment and Suspended Sediment
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Storms transport eroded soil and debris. Moving water carries suspended sediment, which may settle in slower water or be resuspended by faster flow. Rainfall context supports investigating sediment runoff; it does not prove that a lake event was caused by runoff.
evidence.applicability: General hydrologic mechanism. Local catchment, flow and field measurements are required to test it.

evidence.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
evidence.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

hypotheses.name: Algal biomass change
support: Chlorophyll proxy: 3.253; previous-period median: 4.994.
hypotheses.limitations: A proxy cannot identify cyanobacteria, toxins or nutrient sources. Nutrient and field measurements are required.

evidence.title: US EPA: Water Treatment Optimization for Cyanotoxins, Version 1.0
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Nutrients, calm water, temperature and light can favor cyanobacteria growth. Rain can supply nutrients, followed by conditions that support growth. A chlorophyll or algae signal does not establish cyanobacteria species, toxins, or exposure risk; confirmation needs appropriate sampling.
evidence.applicability: General bloom context, not a calibration for this satellite chlorophyll proxy or a local bloom diagnosis. See source section 2 and Table 2-1.

hypotheses.name: Measurement or coverage artefact
support: Satellite pixel coverage is unknown; valid uploaded measurements are retained with this qualification.
hypotheses.limitations: Low coverage suggests inspecting imagery; it does not establish that the observed change is an artefact. Adequate coverage does not rule out atmospheric errors.

evidence.title: NASA MODIS surface reflectance quality flags in Earth Engine
evidence.text: Paraphrase: The MOD09GA product documents surface-reflectance quality information, including cloud state, cloud shadow, land and water flags, aerosol conditions and band quality. These fields support checking observation reliability before interpreting spectral changes. The supplied CSV lacks those QA fields and does not identify its source product.
evidence.applicability: MODIS quality-control context only. This reference does not establish that the uploaded CSV was extracted from MOD09GA, that its pixels were cloud-masked, or that its turbidity and chlorophyll values have calibrated physical units.

hypotheses.name: Seasonal variation
support: 7 usable periods near the same season last year.
hypotheses.limitations: A single seasonal window is not enough to establish a recurring seasonal cause. Compare several years and model residuals.

evidence.title: USGS: Sediment and Suspended Sediment
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Storms transport eroded soil and debris. Moving water carries suspended sediment, which may settle in slower water or be resuspended by faster flow. Rainfall context supports investigating sediment runoff; it does not prove that a lake event was caused by runoff.

evidence.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
evidence.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

evidence.applicability: General hydrologic mechanism. Local catchment, flow and field measurements are required to test it.

evidence.title: USGS: Turbidity and Water
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Turbidity describes optical clarity. Suspended sediment, algae and other material can increase it. Rainfall runoff can wash particles into water; high flows can also resuspend sediment. A turbidity increase alone does not identify its cause.
evidence.applicability: General mechanisms; USGS describes turbidity measurements. This prototype uses an uncalibrated satellite proxy, not NTU. No local causal or safety determination.

hypotheses.name: Algal biomass change
support: Chlorophyll proxy: 9.298; previous-period median: 4.457.
hypotheses.limitations: A proxy cannot identify cyanobacteria, toxins or nutrient sources. Nutrient and field measurements are required.

evidence.title: US EPA: Water Treatment Optimization for Cyanotoxins, Version 1.0
evidence.text: Paraphrase: Nutrients, calm water, temperature and light can favor cyanobacteria growth. Rain can supply nutrients, followed by conditions that support growth. A chlorophyll or algae signal does not establish cyanobacteria species, toxins, or exposure risk; confirmation needs appropriate sampling.
evidence.applicability: General bloom context, not a calibration for this satellite chlorophyll proxy or a local bloom diagnosis. See source section 2 and Table 2-1.

hypotheses.name: Measurement or coverage artefact
support: Satellite pixel coverage is unknown; valid uploaded measurements are retained with this qualification.
hypotheses.limitations: Low coverage suggests inspecting imagery; it does not establish that the observed change is an artefact. Adequate coverage does not rule out atmospheric errors.

evidence.title: NASA MODIS surface reflectance quality flags in Earth Engine
evidence.text: Paraphrase: The MOD09GA product documents surface-reflectance quality information, including cloud state, cloud shadow, land and water flags, aerosol conditions and band quality. These fields support checking observation reliability before interpreting spectral changes. The supplied CSV lacks those QA fields and does not identify its source product.
evidence.applicability: MODIS quality-control context only. This reference does not establish that the uploaded CSV was extracted from MOD09GA, that its pixels were cloud-masked, or that its turbidity and chlorophyll values have calibrated physical units.

hypotheses.name: Seasonal variation
support: 7 usable periods near the same season last year.
hypotheses.limitations: A single seasonal window is not enough to establish a recurring seasonal cause. Compare several years and model residuals.
